headline: TALAMORE LOCKS C$620M COFFEE PROJECT FINANCING — STIFEL + BMO LEAD C$100M EQUITY, YUKON HEAP-LEACH GOLD MOVES TO 2027 CONSTRUCTION DECISION (TSXV:TALA)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV:TALA)
snippet: Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV:TALA) announced July 5, 2026 a comprehensive C$620 million total construction financing package for its 100%-owned Coffee Gold Project in Yukon, Canada — originally acquired from Newmont — advancing the project from exploration-stage asset to development-ready open-pit heap-leach operation. The package comprises: a C$100 million equity component led by Stifel and BMO Capital Markets (including a C$30 million cash portion on hand), a committed debt facility from a syndicate of Canadian banks, and warrant coverage. Early works are underway; a formal construction decision is targeted for H1 2027. Coffee is a large-footprint, low-grade heap-leach gold deposit in Yukon's Dawson Range, a jurisdiction that has historically faced permitting complexity but where the Yukon government has signaled expedited processing for fully financed development projects. For junior mining investors, a TSX-V listed developer that has assembled C$620M of committed financing against a Yukon heap-leach gold asset at $4,183/oz — a gold price that delivers substantially improved heap-leach economics relative to any prior feasibility assumptions — represents a meaningful late-cycle development catalyst: from financing close to a construction decision inside 12 months, the stock de-risks along a clear milestone path rather than remaining subject to the discretion of a single major partner.

headline: PHOENIX METALS C$42.5M IPO PRICES TODAY — BC GOLD-COPPER JUNIOR UPSIZED, TRADES ON TSX JULY 6 AT $1.25/SHARE (TSX:PCA)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Phoenix Metals Corp. (TSX:PCA)
snippet: Phoenix Metals Corp. (TSX:PCA) priced and upsized its initial public offering on July 6, 2026 to C$42.5 million at $1.25 per share — issuing 34 million common shares — and filed a supplemented PREP prospectus, with trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange commencing today under the symbol PCA. The company holds a portfolio of gold-copper exploration assets in south-central British Columbia, a jurisdiction that has delivered several major porphyry copper-gold discoveries over the last decade including Newcrest's Red Chris expansion and Freeport's Galore Creek. Phoenix is entering the public market with a fully funded initial program at a moment when BC porphyry copper-gold exploration is receiving elevated institutional attention driven by the Section 232 copper tariff structure and sustained gold above $4,000/oz. For retail junior mining investors, today's TSX listing means Phoenix moves from private to fully liquid, with a clean share structure, C$42.5M in the treasury, and a BC exploration mandate at the start of the summer drilling season. The combination of a gold-copper porphyry focus in a prime Canadian jurisdiction and a fully funded IPO — upsized, not downsized — signals meaningful institutional demand ahead of the 2026 drill program.

headline: ALKANE COSTERFIELD TRUE BLUE: 84.1 G/T AU AND 15.4% ANTIMONY — CHINA EXPORT-BANNED CRITICAL MINERAL IN VICTORIA HIGH-GRADE VEIN SYSTEM (TSX:ALK)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Alkane Resources Ltd. (TSX:ALK)
snippet: Alkane Resources Ltd. (TSX:ALK / ASX:ALK) reported July 5, 2026 further high-grade gold-antimony drill results from infill and extension drilling at its True Blue deposit, located 2 kilometres west of active underground workings at the Costerfield Operation in central Victoria, Australia. An additional 33 holes targeted the Freeman veining system; standout assays from the Freeman 700 vein include 57.6 g/t gold and 25.4% antimony over 0.25 metres in hole TB055, 20.9 g/t gold and 19.5% antimony over 0.31 metres in TB057, and 30.1 g/t gold and 14.8% antimony over 0.25 metres in TB065. Associated veins returned 84.1 g/t gold and 15.4% antimony over 0.48 metres in TB084. The antimony context is material: China imposed export restrictions on refined antimony in September 2024, and antimony — used in ammunition primers, military flame retardants, and advanced battery systems — is now classed as a strategic critical mineral by the U.S., EU, and Canada, with no comparable Western primary source in production. True Blue's grades confirm a high-value gold-antimony vein system at shallow depth; the infill program has now given Alkane geological confidence to proceed with development planning, with continued drilling targeting along-strike extensions to the north and south. For investors tracking dual-commodity critical mineral exposures, True Blue's combination of exceptional gold grades and strategic antimony at an operating Australian mine represents a genuinely differentiated asset.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,000 AHEAD OF FOMC MINUTES JULY 8 — US DEBT LOAD FORCING CENTRAL BANK GOLD ACCUMULATION; WARSH DOT-PLOT SHIFTS DECISIVE CATALYST
snippet: FXLeaders published a July 5, 2026 gold market analysis framing the FOMC meeting minutes release on July 8 as the most significant near-term catalyst for gold direction since the June 17 meeting that elevated the rate-hike dot-plot. Gold closed the week ending July 3 at $4,175.70 — recording its first weekly gain in five weeks following the June 57,000-job NFP miss — but FXLeaders identifies the real driver as structural rather than cyclical: a US federal debt load that crossed $36 trillion in mid-2026 is compelling foreign central banks to accelerate reserve diversification into gold regardless of short-term rate path. The June FOMC under Chair Kevin Warsh removed forward guidance language and shifted the median 2026 dot to imply a single 25-basis-point hike, with September hike probability now at 50% following the NFP miss. FXLeaders argues the minutes text will either confirm hawkish unity (bearish for gold near-term) or reveal dissent from the dot-plot shift (bullish). At $4,186.38 as of July 6, gold remains in a technical no-man's land between $4,000 support and $4,460 primary resistance; the FOMC minutes are the swing factor. For retail investors monitoring entry points following the Q2 correction from $5,405, the week of July 7–11 — incorporating FOMC minutes and initial jobless claims — is the first clear near-term catalyst window of H2 2026.

headline: BATTERY METALS RECOVERY HITS EV SPEED BUMP — DRC COBALT BAN AND INDONESIA QUOTAS LIFT PRICES BUT CHINA EV SALES FALL 15%, NORTH AMERICA -25%
snippet: A July 5, 2026 Mining.com analysis by Andy Home confirms that the two-year battery metals bear market has run its course — lithium, cobalt, and nickel have all recovered substantially from their 2024–2025 lows — but a stop-start EV market is complicating the recovery thesis for junior battery metals investors. Supply restraint has driven the rebound: the Democratic Republic of Congo banned cobalt exports in February 2025; Indonesia imposed nickel quotas to rein in oversupply from its mining sector; and China suspended the giant Jianxiawo lithium mine, removing a significant swing supply source. Battery-grade lithium carbonate spot prices have recovered to approximately $24,000/mt from sub-$7,000 lows. However, the demand side is bifurcating: after surging 20% year-on-year in 2025, global EV sales grew only 0.9% in January–May 2026; North American EV sales fell 25% year-on-year; China — the dominant market — contracted 15% in the same period. The battery chemistry shift further complicates the picture: lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries, which contain neither cobalt nor nickel, now hold 50% global market share in energy storage applications. For retail investors tracking battery metals juniors, the analysis reframes the sector into three tiers: lithium (recovering via supply discipline, LFP remains a tailwind); cobalt (export ban supports floor, but EV softness caps recovery); and nickel (quota-constrained Indonesia means floor, but LFP displaces cathode demand). Grid storage — the structural growth driver — prioritizes LFP, leaving cobalt and nickel dependent on EV adoption acceleration that has stalled in key markets.

headline: GOLD SEASONAL LAUNCHPAD: HAMILTON MAPS 23 BULL-YEAR SUMMERS — JUNE 2013 PARALLEL, $3,993 FLOOR, SEASONAL BASE SETS LATE JULY (GOLDSEEK)
snippet: Adam Hamilton of Zeal LLC published 'Gold Seasonal Launchpad' on GoldSeek on July 3, 2026, presenting a quantitative seasonal analysis of gold's historical July–August performance across 23 modern gold bull market years. The analysis identifies gold's June 2026 correction — an 11.6% decline that was the worst single-month drop since October 2008 — as an extreme that historically sets up a strong seasonal base. Gold bottomed at $3,993 on June 24, touching below $4,000 for the first time since early Q1 2026. Hamilton draws the most direct parallel to June 2013: gold dropped 11.5% in June 2013 amid the taper tantrum, then staged a significant recovery through July before resuming the corrective bear. The distinction he draws for 2026: unlike 2013 (when the gold bull market was definitively over and real rates were rising sharply), the 2026 correction occurred within a structurally intact bull market driven by central bank buying rather than speculative Western positioning — meaning the seasonal base-building pattern is more likely to be followed by a genuine recovery leg than a dead-cat bounce. The seasonal data shows gold firms from early July into early August in the majority of historical bull-market years. For retail investors who missed the $4,000 entry window at the June 24 low, Hamilton's framework suggests late July — the deepest part of the seasonal pressure window — as the next high-probability accumulation zone before the sector typically re-accelerates into Q4.
